key_idea: A reflection maps centroid to centroid, so the mirror must be the perpendicular bisector of the two centroids: only one candidate line to verify.
sketch: If the centroids coincide the answer is impossible (the mirror would pass through the centroid, which lies inside the hull of a set that must be strictly on one side). Otherwise take d = primitive direction of SB-SA and the line through (SA+SB)/(2n) perpendicular to d; for each point of A check it is strictly on A's side, reflect it exactly in integer arithmetic (require divisibility) and binary-search it in sorted B. Injectivity makes n successful lookups a set equality. O(n log n). Pitfalls: stay in exact arithmetic (__int128, values reach ~1e30 after scaling by 2n), and do not forget the separation condition, since sets can be mirror images while interleaved across the line. Stress-tested against a brute force over all candidate bisectors with fractions.
